prd.problem: The prototype map is a 15-by-10 schematic SVG with invented terrain (crates/cna-sim/src/lib.rs COLS/ROWS/terrain()), not the Campaign for North Africa battlefield. Players need the supplied CNA map rendered as a draggable, zoomable tiled surface with calibrated hexes and source-backed gameplay geography; the simulation and movement builders need a stable, versioned geometry and terrain contract they can consume before the full map is finished.
prd.why_now: docs/CNAv2.1.0 now supplies 'CNA Map Vassal Mitch Guthrie 2021.png' (verified 14310x4632 px) and six VASSAL HexGrid definitions in buildFile.xml (Malta plus map sections A-E; dx 72.95, dy 85.25, sideways, per-section x0/y0 and numbering offsets hOff 2-21, vOff -1 to -133). Zone polygons imply roughly 71 Malta, 1001 A, 1974 B, 1534 C, 1254 D and 1306 E hex cells (about 7140 including sea). These are calibration evidence, not a terrain database. Graziani's Offensive (SC21 60.31/60.41) deploys units on all five sections (A4829 Benina through E3815 Aboukir), so the first certified scenario needs the whole board's geometry and a reviewed C/D/E corridor. Publishing the contract and a fixture first lets the other three orbs proceed in parallel.
prd.users: Campaign players; the simulation builder consuming hex IDs, adjacency, terrain and hexside features; the movement builder consuming hex centers, shared-edge normals, hit testing and screen transforms through a published overlay API; the catalog orb is not a consumer.
prd.value: One map orb owns map-source provenance, the new crates/cna-map contract crate, tile generation, crates/frontend/src/map.rs viewport rendering, the calibrated hex overlay and terrain/hexside transcription. Milestones in order: (E1) source census and geometry contract with a consumer fixture; (E2) tile pipeline and draggable viewport with an overlay API for movement; (E3) calibrated full-board hex overlay and seam/errata adjudication; (E4) transcription tooling, the certified-subset validator and the Graziani C/D/E corridor plus board-wide point features; (E5) remaining board, Malta and off-map boxes; (E6) gameplay-map acceptance including validation of every hex reference printed in the scenario rules and a checksummed release. No map leaf depends on simulation rules, movement playback or catalog work; the only upstream dependency is the simulation-owned shared scaffold leaf that adds crates/cna-map to the workspace and splits frontend files by owner. Shared entry points (Cargo.toml, package.json, crates/frontend/src/lib.rs, index.html, .agents/setup) are edited only by the simulation integration owner.
success_metrics: crates/cna-map v1 defines HexId (section letter + printed XXYY, e.g. C3926), parse/display round trip, six-direction adjacency including cross-section seams, hex centers and corners in board pixels, shared-edge segments with outward-normal bearings, board-to-screen transforms and terrain/hexside record types; docs/contracts/map-v1.md and a fixture are published before any consumer integration leaf starts.

The full 14310x4632 battlefield pans and zooms through tiles with a recorded budget (decoded tiles, time to first tile, peak JS heap) measured in pinned Chromium at 2458x1358 and 1280x800; the full-resolution image is never decoded as a single bitmap in the browser.

All six source grids are reconciled against at least five printed anchor hexes per section and every seam; residuals are recorded in docs/map/calibration.md, and ambiguous cells plus the Sep 79 D2228/2328 escarpment correction have adjudication records.
Hex outlines are slightly more visible at gameplay zoom than today; outline and hit testing stay aligned during pan, zoom and resize at 2458x1358 (browser test samples centers and near-edge points).

Every playable cell and relevant hexside has a reviewed record or an explicit unresolved/provisional status; an integrity test fails if a certified scenario subset contains an unreviewed cell or untranscribed area defaults to clear desert.
Every hex reference printed on SC21 text pages resolves to a valid HexId or is listed as an unresolved source error; the subset validator (E4.I1.S3) is published for the simulation to call.
Map leaves have only earlier prerequisites; the combined manifest check (python3 docs/planning/cna-dag-check.py) passes with no cycles or backward stage edges.
out_of_scope: Combat arithmetic, movement legality and costs, supply consumption and victory rules (simulation owns these; map supplies terrain facts only).
Unit facing animation and selected/hover unit styling (movement owns these through the overlay API).

Treating the VASSAL grid, zone polygons, v2.1 map labels or image colours as authoritative per-hex terrain; they are evidence reviewed against the rules' Terrain Effects Chart (L21 8.37) and the printed map.
Redistributing source map art or generated tiles in a public build without a recorded permission decision; local research use is not a redistribution grant.
Editing simulation-, catalog- or movement-owned files; boundary changes are requested from the owning orb.
open_questions: BLOCKER for public distribution only: what permission covers redistribution of the SPI/White Box/VASSAL-derived map artwork ((c) 1979 SPI / (c) 2022 White Box Games per moduledata)? Until Kevin records a decision, tiles stay in ignored public/tiles and production builds exclude them.

Which printed/source discrepancies (seam duplicates, mismatched numbering, VASSAL v2.1 added dumps/fortification labels) need Kevin's adjudication? E3.I1.S3 produces the list; terrain work proceeds with provisional status meanwhile.
Global order: map E1 publishes contracts in stage 0, simulation and movement consume them, and the map never waits for a downstream consumer.

scope: Sources: VBF (docs/CNAv2.1.0/buildFile.xml)

crates/cna-map/src/geometry.rs: center(HexId) -> BoardPoint, corners(HexId) -> [BoardPoint; 6], edge(HexsideId) -> (BoardPoint, BoardPoint), edge_normal_bearing(HexId, Direction) in degrees clockwise from screen east, hex_at(BoardPoint) -> Option<HexId>.
Derive from each section's dx/dy/x0/y0/sideways; document orientation (flat- vs pointy-top) with a diagram in docs/contracts/map-v1.md.
Expose the six possible travel bearings as constants so consumers never recompute them.
acceptance_criteria: For every fixture hex, hex_at(center(h)) == h and points 1 px inside each edge midpoint resolve to h.
Edge normal of (h, d) is perpendicular (dot product < 1e-9) to the shared edge and points from h toward neighbour(h, d).
Adjacent centers differ by the same bearing as the shared-edge normal (tolerance 0.01 degrees).

scope: Sources: AL21 (docs/CNAv2.1.0/Rules_Air&Logistics_07-2021.pdf) 55.3; SC21 (docs/CNAv2.1.0/Rules_Scenarios_07-2021.pdf) 60.7, 61.6, 62.5, 63.7; VCL (docs/CNAv2.1.0/changelog.txt, playnotes.txt, Read me.txt) v2.1 Map; VIMG (docs/CNAv2.1.0/images/) 55.3 Port Capacity and Efficiency Level Chart.png

epics.title: Gameplay-map acceptance and release
epics.objective: Validate every scenario hex reference, pass browser acceptance and publish a checksummed map-v1.1 data release.
epics.user_value: The simulation can certify scenarios knowing every referenced hex exists and its geography status is known.
acceptance_criteria: All SC21 text-page hex references resolve or are recorded as source errors.
Browser acceptance screenshots inspected.
map-v1.1 release with checksums and honest unresolved counts.

issues.title: Scenario hex-reference validation
issues.summary: Extract every hex reference from the scenario rules and validate it.
issues.approach: Parse a checked-in `pdftotext -raw` extract of SC21 for [A-E]dddd patterns plus named locations; OCR-damaged IDs (e.g. '84827' for Benghazi B4827) are mapped only through reviewed correction entries.
risks: Image-only scenario pages (SC21 pp.6, 9-10, 12-16) hide references; the simulation re-validates them through the published validator when it transcribes those pages.
acceptance_criteria: Hex-reference report exists and is enforced by a test.

subissues.title: Extract and resolve every printed scenario hex reference
subissues.goal: Prove no scenario text names a hex the map lacks.
scope: Sources: SC21 (docs/CNAv2.1.0/Rules_Scenarios_07-2021.pdf) 60-64; L21 (docs/CNAv2.1.0/Rules_Land_07-2021.pdf) 4.43 reinforcement schedules

crates/cna-map/src/bin/scenario-hexrefs.rs reads docs/map/scenario-hexrefs.txt (generated with `pdftotext -raw` from SC21 and checked in as a cited derived extract) and resolves each reference; writes docs/map/scenario-hexrefs.md with unresolved and OCR-corrected entries.
Named places (Bardia, Tobruk, Alexandria, Tripoli, Tripolitania, Cairo/Helwan) resolve through point features or off-map boxes.
non_goals: Image-only pages (re-validated by simulation setup leaves).
acceptance_criteria: Every reference from SC21 text pages 3-5, 7-8, 11 and 17 resolves or is listed with a reason; the test fails on any new unresolved reference.
The report names the image-only pages it does not cover.

issues.title: Browser acceptance and versioned release
issues.summary: Final visual acceptance and data release for consumers.
issues.approach: Screenshots and a checksummed data release; no simulation-rules dependency.
risks: Unresolved counts must be shown honestly in the release notes.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance screenshots inspected and release published in-repo.

subissues.title: Map browser acceptance pass
subissues.goal: Confirm the finished map experience visually and functionally.
scope: Cross-project prerequisites (enforced by docs/planning/cna-dag.manifest.json): cna-simulation:E1.I1.S2 (npm run test:browser harness)
Browser tour: full-board overview, gameplay zoom on Tobruk, Bardia, Matruh, Alexandria and Benghazi; grid toggle; a hex info panel showing only map facts and review status for the hovered hex.
Screenshots at 2458x1358 and 1280x800 saved under tests/browser/__screenshots__/map/ and inspected.
acceptance_criteria: All tour steps pass; inspected screenshots show no seams, misaligned outlines or missing tiles.

subissues.title: map-v1.1 data release and uncertainty report
subissues.goal: Hand consumers a versioned, checksummed geography release.
scope: Write public/data/map/map-v1.json (or per-section files) with checksums in public/data/map/release.json; docs/map/release-notes.md lists reviewed/provisional/unresolved counts by section and open adjudications.
Tag contract version 1.1 in docs/contracts/map-v1.md.
non_goals: Changing contract types (a breaking change needs a new major version and a forward simulation leaf).
acceptance_criteria: release.json checksums match files (test).
Release-note counts equal the terrain_integrity report.
